analysis.title: Marketcolour + Coreweave / Infineon / Siemens Energy / Zalando / FLS / ABN
key_insights: US equities closed lower on 11 Nov 2026 after a hot CPI print of +30bps vs consensus of +20bps, the third consecutive month with a 0.1% beat. SPX -38bps to 7520, NDX -60bps to 27740, RTY -68bps to 2821.
The 2Y UST had its worst day since Oct 2024. 5 of 11 S&P sectors rose, Financials +0.49% and Tech -1.40%. NDX weakness was concentrated in Semis, Memory and Neoclouds.

GS floor activity was a 5 on a 1-10 scale. Asset managers were moderate net sellers, driven by supply in large cap tech. Hedge funds were net sellers, with shorts exceeding longs, concentrated in tech and macro products.

GS now expects a second 25bp Fed hike in December and adds a third 25bp hike to its forecast for March 2027. A January hike is possible, but March is seen as more likely because GS expects softer November and December inflation reports followed by larger start-of-year price increases.

CoreWeave rose 8% post market and GS would add to positions. 4Q implied revenue guidance is 3% above the Street, margins are 100bps above and capex is 22% below. There will be no additional parent-level unsecured debt through 2027. Other financing levers are customer prepayments, OEM financing and growing operating cash flow.

CoreWeave 4-5yr contracts now price at $20-$25mn/MW, against WholeCo revenue/MW of about $10mn and capex of about $40mn/MW. GS now estimates unlevered IRR of 20-30% before residual value, up from 15-21%.

Infineon is rated BUY with a PT of EUR91 (85% upside). GS raises FY27-30 revenue estimates by about 2-3% on AI power semis demand in the PS segment and better ATV demand, and raises gross margin estimates by 0-1pp. Adj. EBIT estimates rise 3-4% and EPS estimates rise 3-4%.

Zalando is rated BUY with a PT of EUR44 (60% upside). After hosting the CFO, GS notes 4Q has started well with autumn/winter trading on track. Overlap across its three B2C apps is 10%. Management stays confident on a 3-4% retail media target by 2028 and reiterated the 6-8% 2028 adj. EBIT margin target. B2B momentum continues with a full Scayle pipeline.

Siemens Energy is rated CL BUY with a PT of EUR212 (70% upside). The announced buyback plus dividends implies EUR27bn of shareholder returns through FY2030, vs Visible Alpha at EUR24bn and GSe at EUR30bn. GS expects the Capital Markets Day on 12 Nov to show a stronger profit outlook and material cash flow acceleration.
Siemens Energy's current capital allocation through FY2028 is 1/3 of cash flow to capex, 1/3 to returns and 1/3 retained. GS expects this to change once FY2030 guidance is added.

FLS 3Q beat. Organic orders rose 32% vs consensus +26% and organic revenue rose 6% vs consensus +4.6%. EBITA beat by 8% with margins 100bps above consensus. Guidance narrowed to growth of +1-3% (prev 0 to 4%) and margins of about 16.5% (prev 16-16.5%, consensus 16.6%).

ABN AMRO 3Q net profit beat by 21pct, helped by higher NII, a one-off other income gain on NIBC and lower loan loss provisions. Revenue was 4pct above consensus. Excluding the one-off, revenue was 1pct better and pre-provision profit beat by 2%. Provisions showed a release due to model updates.

ITV missed and guided below as digital ad revenue slowed. 3Q26 revenue missed consensus by 1%. TV advertising revenue fell 8% vs guidance of around 5%. Digital advertising growth slowed to 6% over nine months from 13% in 1H.

INWIT 3Q26 results were in line with consensus and 2026 guidance was reiterated. Italian authorities are looking to accelerate resolution of the contract disputes with Swisscom and Telecom Italia, which could shorten the period of uncertainty.

earnings_insights: CoreWeave (reported 11 Nov, shares +8% post market): 4Q implied revenue guidance 3% above the Street, margins 100bps above, capex 22% below. Basis for the Street comparison is not specified in the report.

Infineon: GS raises FY27-30 revenue estimates by about 2-3%, gross margin estimates by 0-1pp, adj. EBIT estimates by 3-4% and EPS estimates by 3-4%. These are GS estimate changes, not reported figures.

FLS 3Q (reported): organic orders +32% vs consensus +26%, organic revenue +6% vs consensus +4.6%, EBITA 8% above consensus with margins 100bps above consensus. Guidance narrowed to growth +1-3% (prev 0 to 4%) and margins about 16.5% (prev 16-16.5%, consensus 16.6%).

ABN AMRO 3Q (reported): net profit beat consensus by 21pct. Revenue was 4pct above consensus, with NII 2pct better, fees 2pct lower and other income 82pct higher. Excluding the NIBC one-off, revenue was 1pct better and pre-provision profit 2% above consensus. Costs were in line.

ITV 3Q26 (reported): revenue missed consensus by 1%. Media & Entertainment was 2% short of consensus. Studios matched consensus but missed GS estimates by 3%. TV advertising revenue fell 8% vs guidance of around 5%. Digital advertising growth was 6% over nine months vs 13% in 1H.
INWIT 3Q26 (reported): results in line with consensus and 2026 guidance reiterated.
Zalando: CFO said 4Q has started well with autumn/winter trading on track. The 6-8% 2028 adj. EBIT margin target was reiterated.
Siemens Energy: GS expects the 12 Nov Capital Markets Day to show a stronger profit outlook. Buyback plus dividends implies EUR27bn of returns through FY2030 vs GSe EUR30bn.

macro_indicators.interpretation: The print came in 10bps above the 20bps consensus, the third consecutive month with a 0.1% beat. The 2Y Treasury yield had its worst day since Oct 2024 and equities fell.
Consensus was 10bps below the actual print.

macro_indicators.reading: Second 25bp hike in December 2026, third 25bp hike in March 2027
macro_indicators.interpretation: GS expects further tightening. A third hike could come in January 2027, but March is seen as more likely.

trade_ideas.rationale: 4Q implied guidance is above the Street on revenue and margins and capex is below. Financing clarity improved and estimated unlevered IRR rose to 20-30%.

risk_factors: A third consecutive 0.1% CPI beat raises the risk of more Fed hikes and rate pressure on equities, especially tech.
Ongoing cost pressures could lift inflation in January 2027 through larger start-of-year price increases.
Digital ad revenue slowdown at ITV, as ad-supported tiers at competitors also slow.

Hedge funds were net sellers with shorts exceeding longs, concentrated in tech and macro products.
